title: The Most Merciful, above the Throne
arabic: ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنُ عَلَى ٱلْعَرْشِ ٱسْتَوَىٰ
translation: The Most Merciful rose over the Throne.
note: Istiwa over the Throne is mentioned in seven passages. In the Athari explanation, it is affirmed as befits Allah, without describing how or comparing Him with His creation. The six companion passages below are excerpts; each link opens the complete verse.

related.title: Istiwa over the Throne
related.arabic: إِنَّ رَبَّكُمُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضَ فِى سِتَّةِ أَيَّامٍ ثُمَّ ٱسْتَوَىٰ عَلَى ٱلْعَرْشِ
related.translation: Your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth in six days, then rose over the Throne.

related.title: Istiwa over the Throne
related.arabic: إِنَّ رَبَّكُمُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضَ فِى سِتَّةِ أَيَّامٍ ثُمَّ ٱسْتَوَىٰ عَلَى ٱلْعَرْشِ
related.translation: Your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth in six days, then rose over the Throne.

related.title: Istiwa over the Throne
related.arabic: ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِى رَفَعَ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٰتِ بِغَيْرِ عَمَدٍ تَرَوْنَهَا ۖ ثُمَّ ٱسْتَوَىٰ عَلَى ٱلْعَرْشِ
related.translation: Allah is the One who raised the heavens without pillars that you see, then rose over the Throne.

related.title: Istiwa over the Throne
related.arabic: ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضَ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا فِى سِتَّةِ أَيَّامٍ ثُمَّ ٱسْتَوَىٰ عَلَى ٱلْعَرْشِ
related.translation: The One who created the heavens, the earth and everything between them in six days, then rose over the Throne.

related.title: Istiwa over the Throne
related.arabic: ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضَ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا فِى سِتَّةِ أَيَّامٍ ثُمَّ ٱسْتَوَىٰ عَلَى ٱلْعَرْشِ
related.translation: Allah is the One who created the heavens, the earth and everything between them in six days, then rose over the Throne.

related.title: Istiwa over the Throne
related.arabic: هُوَ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضَ فِى سِتَّةِ أَيَّامٍ ثُمَّ ٱسْتَوَىٰ عَلَى ٱلْعَرْشِ
related.translation: He is the One who created the heavens and the earth in six days, then rose over the Throne.

title: The One in heaven
arabic: ءَأَمِنتُم مَّن فِى ٱلسَّمَآءِ أَن يَخْسِفَ بِكُمُ ٱلْأَرْضَ فَإِذَا هِىَ تَمُورُ
translation: Do you feel safe from the One in heaven causing the earth to swallow you, and then it begins to shake?
note: The wording is man fi al-samaʾ. In the Athari explanation, this affirms Allah’s highness; it does not mean that the created heavens surround or contain Him.

related.title: The warning continues
related.arabic: أَمْ أَمِنتُم مَّن فِى ٱلسَّمَآءِ أَن يُرْسِلَ عَلَيْكُمْ حَاصِبًا ۖ فَسَتَعْلَمُونَ كَيْفَ نَذِيرِ
related.translation: Or do you feel safe from the One in heaven sending a storm of stones against you? Then you will know what My warning is like.

title: They fear their Lord above them
arabic: يَخَافُونَ رَبَّهُم مِّن فَوْقِهِمْ وَيَفْعَلُونَ مَا يُؤْمَرُونَ ۩
translation: They fear their Lord above them and carry out what they are commanded.
note: The preceding verse mentions the creatures of the heavens and earth and the angels prostrating to Allah.

title: Good words ascend to Him
arabic: إِلَيْهِ يَصْعَدُ ٱلْكَلِمُ ٱلطَّيِّبُ وَٱلْعَمَلُ ٱلصَّـٰلِحُ يَرْفَعُهُۥ
translation: To Him the good word ascends, and righteous work raises it.
note: This excerpt directly states that good words ascend to Him. The relationship of “righteous work” to “raises it” has more than one explanation in tafsir; the quoted evidence here is the preceding clause of ascent.

title: The angels and the Spirit ascend to Him
arabic: تَعْرُجُ ٱلْمَلَـٰٓئِكَةُ وَٱلرُّوحُ إِلَيْهِ فِى يَوْمٍ كَانَ مِقْدَارُهُۥ خَمْسِينَ أَلْفَ سَنَةٍ
translation: The angels and the Spirit ascend to Him in a day whose measure is fifty thousand years.
note: The Spirit is understood here as Jibril. The text explicitly says “to Him”.

related.title: Lord of the ways of ascent
related.translation: From Allah, Lord of the ways of ascent.
related.note: This verse continues the sentence beginning in 70:1–2.

title: Allah raised ʿIsa to Himself
arabic: بَل رَّفَعَهُ ٱللَّهُ إِلَيْهِ ۚ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ عَزِيزًا حَكِيمًا
translation: Rather, Allah raised him to Himself. Allah is mighty and wise.
note: The preceding verses speak about ʿIsa, son of Maryam. The phrase “to Himself” is the point cited here.

related.title: The promise to ʿIsa
related.note: A short excerpt from Allah’s address to ʿIsa. The complete verse is linked.

title: The affair ascends to Him
arabic: يُدَبِّرُ ٱلْأَمْرَ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ إِلَى ٱلْأَرْضِ ثُمَّ يَعْرُجُ إِلَيْهِ فِى يَوْمٍ كَانَ مِقْدَارُهُۥٓ أَلْفَ سَنَةٍ مِّمَّا تَعُدُّونَ
translation: He directs the affair from heaven to earth; then it ascends to Him in a day whose measure is a thousand years by your reckoning.
note: This passage follows the statement of creation and istiwa in 32:4.

title: Above His servants
arabic: وَهُوَ ٱلْقَاهِرُ فَوْقَ عِبَادِهِۦ ۚ وَهُوَ ٱلْحَكِيمُ ٱلْخَبِيرُ
translation: He is the Subduer above His servants, and He is the Wise, the Fully Aware.
note: This affirms His supremacy over His servants. Athari scholars read this with the more explicit texts of highness and istiwa.

title: Your Lord, the Most High
arabic: سَبِّحِ ٱسْمَ رَبِّكَ ٱلْأَعْلَى
translation: Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High.

title: Al-ʿAliyy, al-ʿAzim
arabic: وَهُوَ ٱلْعَلِىُّ ٱلْعَظِيمُ
translation: And He is the Most High, the Magnificent.
note: The closing words of Ayat al-Kursi. His name al-ʿAliyy is read together with the other texts concerning His highness.

title: All that is in the heavens and earth belongs to Him
arabic: لَهُۥ مَا فِى ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ ۖ وَهُوَ ٱلْعَلِىُّ ٱلْعَظِيمُ
translation: To Him belongs everything in the heavens and everything on earth, and He is the Most High, the Magnificent.

title: Pharaoh’s challenge concerning the God of Musa
arabic: وَقَالَ فِرْعَوْنُ يَـٰهَـٰمَـٰنُ ٱبْنِ لِى صَرْحًا لَّعَلِّىٓ أَبْلُغُ ٱلْأَسْبَـٰبَ
translation: Pharaoh said, “Haman, build me a tower so that I may reach the ways.”
note: These are Pharaoh’s words, quoted by the Qur’an in condemnation of his arrogance. Athari authors cite his attempted ascent in their discussion of Musa’s message; this is contextual evidence, not an endorsement of Pharaoh’s reasoning.

related.title: The Qur’an condemns his scheme
related.arabic: أَسْبَـٰبَ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٰتِ فَأَطَّلِعَ إِلَىٰٓ إِلَـٰهِ مُوسَىٰ وَإِنِّى لَأَظُنُّهُۥ كَـٰذِبًا ۚ وَكَذَٰلِكَ زُيِّنَ لِفِرْعَوْنَ سُوٓءُ عَمَلِهِۦ وَصُدَّ عَنِ ٱلسَّبِيلِ ۚ وَمَا كَيْدُ فِرْعَوْنَ إِلَّا فِى تَبَابٍ
related.translation: “The ways of the heavens, so that I may look upon the God of Musa; indeed, I consider him a liar.” Thus Pharaoh’s evil conduct was made attractive to him, and he was turned from the way. Pharaoh’s scheme brought only ruin.

title: Nothing is like Him
arabic: لَيْسَ كَمِثْلِهِۦ شَىْءٌ ۖ وَهُوَ ٱلسَّمِيعُ ٱلْبَصِيرُ
translation: Nothing is like Him, and He is the Hearing, the Seeing.
note: Affirming an attribute does not justify imagining a bodily form, comparing Allah with creation, or claiming to know its modality.

title: Above the Throne — and with you
arabic: هُوَ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضَ فِى سِتَّةِ أَيَّامٍ ثُمَّ ٱسْتَوَىٰ عَلَى ٱلْعَرْشِ ۚ يَعْلَمُ مَا يَلِجُ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَمَا يَخْرُجُ مِنْهَا وَمَا يَنزِلُ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَمَا يَعْرُجُ فِيهَا ۖ وَهُوَ مَعَكُمْ أَيْنَ مَا كُنتُمْ ۚ وَٱللَّهُ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ
translation: He is the One who created the heavens and the earth in six days, then rose over the Throne. He knows what enters the earth and what comes out of it, what descends from heaven and what ascends into it. He is with you wherever you are, and Allah sees all that you do.
note: The same verse affirms istiwa, His complete knowledge, and His being with His servants. Athari scholars affirm all of these together: His maʿiyyah does not mean that He is mixed into His creation.

title: His knowledge encompasses every private conversation
arabic: أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَعْلَمُ مَا فِى ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ ۖ مَا يَكُونُ مِن نَّجْوَىٰ ثَلَـٰثَةٍ إِلَّا هُوَ رَابِعُهُمْ وَلَا خَمْسَةٍ إِلَّا هُوَ سَادِسُهُمْ وَلَآ أَدْنَىٰ مِن ذَٰلِكَ وَلَآ أَكْثَرَ إِلَّا هُوَ مَعَهُمْ أَيْنَ مَا كَانُوا۟ ۖ ثُمَّ يُنَبِّئُهُم بِمَا عَمِلُوا۟ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَـٰمَةِ ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ بِكُلِّ شَىْءٍ عَلِيمٌ
translation: Do you not see that Allah knows everything in the heavens and on earth? No three people speak privately without Him being their fourth, nor five without Him being their sixth; neither fewer nor more than that without Him being with them wherever they are. Then He will tell them what they did on the Day of Resurrection. Allah knows every thing.
note: The verse begins and ends with Allah’s knowledge. The reported early explanations in the consensus section understand this general maʿiyyah in light of His all-encompassing knowledge.

title: They cannot encompass Him in knowledge
arabic: يَعْلَمُ مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمَا خَلْفَهُمْ وَلَا يُحِيطُونَ بِهِۦ عِلْمًا
translation: He knows what is before them and what is behind them, while they do not encompass Him in knowledge.
note: Knowledge of the revealed words is not a claim to know the unseen “how” of Allah’s attributes.

title: He is near and answers the caller
arabic: وَإِذَا سَأَلَكَ عِبَادِى عَنِّى فَإِنِّى قَرِيبٌ ۖ أُجِيبُ دَعْوَةَ ٱلدَّاعِ إِذَا دَعَانِ ۖ فَلْيَسْتَجِيبُوا۟ لِى وَلْيُؤْمِنُوا۟ بِى لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْشُدُونَ
translation: When My servants ask you about Me, I am near. I answer the call of the one who calls upon Me. So let them respond to Me and believe in Me, so that they may be rightly guided.
note: His highness does not mean absence, ignorance of His servants, or inability to hear them. His nearness and response are also affirmed as He has revealed.

title: None is comparable to Him
arabic: وَلَمْ يَكُن لَّهُۥ كُفُوًا أَحَدٌۢ
translation: And no one is comparable to Him.
note: The Creator is not measured by the properties of His creation.

title: The question put to the believing slave woman
arabic: فَقَالَ لَهَا «أَيْنَ اللَّهُ». قَالَتْ فِي السَّمَاءِ. قَالَ «مَنْ أَنَا». قَالَتْ أَنْتَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ. قَالَ «أَعْتِقْهَا فَإِنَّهَا مُؤْمِنَةٌ».
translation: He asked her, ‘Where is Allah?’ She replied, ‘In heaven.’ He asked, ‘Who am I?’ She replied, ‘You are Allah’s Messenger.’ He said, ‘Set her free, for she is a believer.’
kind: Prophetic speech, with the woman’s answers and the Prophet’s approval
note: An excerpt from the report of Muʿawiyah. The Prophet treated his striking of the enslaved shepherdess as grave, before asking her these questions. The answer is fi al-samaʾ: Athari scholars understand it as highness, without containment in the created heavens.

title: Nothing is above You
arabic: وَأَنْتَ الظَّاهِرُ فَلَيْسَ فَوْقَكَ شَىْءٌ
translation: You are al-Ẓāhir, and there is nothing above You.
narrator: Abū Hurayrah; transmitted through Abū Ṣāliḥ and Suhayl
note: An excerpt from the supplication before sleep. The divine name al-Zahir is retained so that the Prophet’s explanation, “nothing is above You”, remains visible. The full supplication also mentions al-Awwal, al-Akhir and al-Batin.

title: The trusted messenger of the One in heaven
arabic: أَلاَ تَأْمَنُونِي وَأَنَا أَمِينُ مَنْ فِي السَّمَاءِ، يَأْتِينِي خَبَرُ السَّمَاءِ صَبَاحًا وَمَسَاءً
translation: Will you not trust me, when I am trusted by the One in heaven, and news from heaven comes to me morning and evening?
note: Spoken after the Prophet’s distribution of gold was questioned. Athari scholars cite man fi al-samaʾ alongside the other texts of highness, without taking the created heaven to enclose Allah.

title: The written book above the Throne
arabic: لَمَّا قَضَى اللَّهُ الْخَلْقَ كَتَبَ فِي كِتَابِهِ، فَهْوَ عِنْدَهُ فَوْقَ الْعَرْشِ إِنَّ رَحْمَتِي غَلَبَتْ غَضَبِي
translation: When Allah completed creation, He wrote in His book—which is with Him above the Throne—‘My mercy has prevailed over My anger.’
kind: Prophetic speech reporting Allah’s written declaration
note: “It is with Him above the Throne” refers grammatically to the written book. Athari scholars cite “with Him above the Throne” as part of the cumulative evidence. The declaration of Allah’s mercy is preserved with the quotation.

title: The descent in the last third of the night
arabic: يَنْزِلُ رَبُّنَا تَبَارَكَ وَتَعَالَى كُلَّ لَيْلَةٍ إِلَى السَّمَاءِ الدُّنْيَا حِينَ يَبْقَى ثُلُثُ اللَّيْلِ الآخِرُ يَقُولُ مَنْ يَدْعُونِي فَأَسْتَجِيبَ لَهُ مَنْ يَسْأَلُنِي فَأُعْطِيَهُ مَنْ يَسْتَغْفِرُنِي فَأَغْفِرَ لَهُ
translation: Our Lord, blessed and exalted, descends each night to the lowest heaven when the final third of the night remains. He says, ‘Who calls upon Me, so that I may answer him? Who asks of Me, so that I may give to him? Who seeks My forgiveness, so that I may forgive him?’
note: The Athari approach affirms this descent as befits Allah, without specifying its modality or likening it to created movement. The report also encourages supplication, asking and repentance in the final third of the night.

title: The angels ascend after attending the prayers
arabic: يَتَعَاقَبُونَ فِيكُمْ مَلاَئِكَةٌ بِاللَّيْلِ وَمَلاَئِكَةٌ بِالنَّهَارِ، وَيَجْتَمِعُونَ فِي صَلاَةِ الْفَجْرِ وَصَلاَةِ الْعَصْرِ، ثُمَّ يَعْرُجُ الَّذِينَ بَاتُوا فِيكُمْ، فَيَسْأَلُهُمْ وَهْوَ أَعْلَمُ بِهِمْ كَيْفَ تَرَكْتُمْ عِبَادِي فَيَقُولُونَ تَرَكْنَاهُمْ وَهُمْ يُصَلُّونَ، وَأَتَيْنَاهُمْ وَهُمْ يُصَلُّونَ
translation: Angels take turns among you by night and by day, meeting at the dawn and afternoon prayers. Then those who spent the night among you ascend. He asks them, although He knows them better, ‘How did you leave My servants?’ They say, ‘We left them praying, and we came to them while they were praying.’
kind: Prophetic speech reporting Allah’s question and the angels’ answer
note: This wording states that the angels ascend and that Allah questions them; it does not add “to Him” after “ascend”. It is supporting evidence alongside more explicit texts, and it affirms that Allah already knows His servants’ condition.

title: The upward gesture at ʿArafah
arabic: قَالُوا نَشْهَدُ أَنَّكَ قَدْ بَلَّغْتَ وَأَدَّيْتَ وَنَصَحْتَ. فَقَالَ بِإِصْبَعِهِ السَّبَّابَةِ يَرْفَعُهَا إِلَى السَّمَاءِ وَيَنْكُتُهَا إِلَى النَّاسِ «اللَّهُمَّ اشْهَدِ اللَّهُمَّ اشْهَدْ». ثَلاَثَ مَرَّاتٍ
translation: They said, ‘We testify that you have conveyed the message, fulfilled your duty and given sincere counsel.’ He then raised his index finger towards heaven and directed it towards the people, saying, ‘O Allah, bear witness; O Allah, bear witness,’ three times.
narrator: Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh; through Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī and Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad
note: From Jabir’s account of the Farewell Pilgrimage, during the sermon at ʿArafah. The upward gesture is the narrator’s description of the Prophet’s action; “O Allah, bear witness” is his speech.

title: Zaynab’s words: above seven heavens
arabic: زَوَّجَكُنَّ أَهَالِيكُنَّ، وَزَوَّجَنِي اللَّهُ تَعَالَى مِنْ فَوْقِ سَبْعِ سَمَوَاتٍ
translation: Your families arranged your marriages, while Allah Most High married me from above seven heavens.
narrator: Anas ibn Mālik, reporting the words of Zaynab bint Jaḥsh
kind: Companion speech: Zaynab bint Jaḥsh, not a direct saying of the Prophet
note: These are Zaynab bint Jahsh’s words, reported by Anas, concerning her marriage mentioned in Qur’an 33:37. They are evidence from a Companion, not a direct saying of the Prophet.

title: The ascent and return to his Lord
arabic: ثُمَّ عَرَجَ بِنَا إِلَى السَّمَاءِ السَّابِعَةِ … فَأَوْحَى اللَّهُ إِلَىَّ مَا أَوْحَى فَفَرَضَ عَلَىَّ خَمْسِينَ صَلاَةً فِي كُلِّ يَوْمٍ وَلَيْلَةٍ فَنَزَلْتُ إِلَى مُوسَى … قَالَ فَرَجَعْتُ إِلَى رَبِّي فَقُلْتُ يَا رَبِّ خَفِّفْ عَلَى أُمَّتِي
translation: Then he took us up to the seventh heaven … Allah revealed to me what He revealed and required of me fifty prayers in every day and night. Then I descended to Moses … He said, ‘I returned to my Lord and said: My Lord, ease the burden upon my community.’
kind: Prophetic narration of the Night Journey and Ascension
note: Ellipses mark separate excerpts from the same narration. Jibril is the one who takes the Prophet upwards. The fuller account includes Ibrahim, the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary and Musa’s advice to seek a reduction in the prayers.

title: The Throne above al-Firdaws
arabic: فَإِذَا سَأَلْتُمُ اللَّهَ فَسَلُوهُ الْفِرْدَوْسَ، فَإِنَّهُ أَوْسَطُ الْجَنَّةِ وَأَعْلَى الْجَنَّةِ، وَفَوْقَهُ عَرْشُ الرَّحْمَنِ، وَمِنْهُ تَفَجَّرُ أَنْهَارُ الْجَنَّةِ
translation: When you ask Allah, ask Him for al-Firdaws: it is the central and highest part of Paradise. Above it is the Throne of the Most Merciful, and from it the rivers of Paradise spring forth.
note: This text places the Throne above al-Firdaws and is read alongside the texts concerning istiwa. Awsat is translated here as “central”; it is also explained as “best”.

title: Deeds are raised to Him
arabic: يُرْفَعُ إِلَيْهِ عَمَلُ اللَّيْلِ قَبْلَ عَمَلِ النَّهَارِ وَعَمَلُ النَّهَارِ قَبْلَ عَمَلِ اللَّيْلِ
translation: The deeds of the night are raised to Him before the deeds of the day, and the deeds of the day before the deeds of the night.
note: An excerpt from the report describing Allah’s freedom from sleep. Here the wording explicitly says that deeds are “raised to Him”. No distance or modality is described.

title: Hands stretched towards heaven in supplication
arabic: ثُمَّ ذَكَرَ الرَّجُلَ يُطِيلُ السَّفَرَ أَشْعَثَ أَغْبَرَ يَمُدُّ يَدَيْهِ إِلَى السَّمَاءِ يَا رَبِّ يَا رَبِّ وَمَطْعَمُهُ حَرَامٌ وَمَشْرَبُهُ حَرَامٌ وَمَلْبَسُهُ حَرَامٌ وَغُذِيَ بِالْحَرَامِ فَأَنَّى يُسْتَجَابُ لِذَلِكَ
translation: Then he mentioned a man on a long journey, dishevelled and dusty, stretching both hands towards heaven: ‘My Lord! My Lord!’ Yet his food is unlawful, his drink is unlawful, his clothing is unlawful, and he has been nourished by what is unlawful. How, then, could his prayer be answered?
kind: Prophetic example, introduced by the narrator
note: Supporting context: the main teaching concerns lawful sustenance and answered supplication. The passage describes hands extended towards heaven in duʿa; that gesture alone is not an independent verbal definition of Allah’s highness.

title: Al-Awzaʿī — الأوزاعي
arabic: كنا والتابعون متوافرون نقول: إن الله تعالى فوق عرشه، ونؤمن بما وردت به السنة من صفاته.
translation: While the Successors were still numerous, we used to say: Allah Most High is above His Throne, and we believe in the attributes reported in the Sunnah.
reference: Al-Dhahabī, Siyar aʿlām al-nubalāʾ, 7:121, biography of al-Awzaʿī; transmitted through al-Bayhaqī's al-Asmāʾ wa-l-ṣifāt.
note: A statement transmitted from al-Awzaʿī, not a Prophetic hadith. Al-Dhahabī records its chain through al-Bayhaqī’s al-Asmāʾ wa-l-ṣifāt. Al-Awzaʿī describes the teaching he knew while the Successors were still numerous.

title: Mālik ibn Anas — مالك بن أنس
arabic: الكيف منه غير معقول، والاستواء منه غير مجهول، والإيمان به واجب، والسؤال عنه بدعة.
translation: Its how is beyond apprehension; His istiwāʾ is not unknown. Belief in it is obligatory, and asking about it [its how] is an innovation.
reference: Al-Dhahabī, Siyar aʿlām al-nubalāʾ, 8:100, biography of Mālik; report of Jaʿfar ibn ʿAbd Allāh.
note: The question in the source is specifically: “How did He perform istiwa?” The answer rejects seeking its manner. This is one transmitted wording; al-Dhahabī also records other versions on the following pages.

title: ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mubārak — عبد الله بن المبارك
arabic: نعرف ربنا بأنه فوق سبع سماوات، على العرش استوى، بائن من خلقه.
translation: We know our Lord as being above seven heavens, having risen over the Throne, distinct from His creation.
reference: Ibn al-Qayyim, Ijtimāʿ al-juyūsh al-islāmiyyah, ed. Zāʾid al-Nushayrī, Dār ʿAṭāʾāt al-ʿIlm / Ibn Ḥazm, 4th ed., 1440/2019, p. 191, 'The statement of ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mubārak'.
note: Reported by ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Shaqīq. The linked edition cites earlier transmissions in ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aḥmad’s al-Sunnah, nos. 22 and 598, and al-Dārimī’s al-Radd ʿalā al-Jahmiyyah, no. 162, and records a sound-chain assessment. The quotation is an excerpt.

title: Abū Ḥātim and Abū Zurʿah al-Rāzī — أبو حاتم وأبو زرعة الرازيان
arabic: وأن الله عز وجل على عرشه بائن من خلقه كما وصف نفسه في كتابه، وعلى لسان رسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم بلا كيف، أحاط بكل شيء علما، ليس كمثله شيء وهو السميع البصير.
translation: Allah, mighty and majestic, is over His Throne, distinct from His creation, as He described Himself in His Book and through His Messenger, without specifying how. His knowledge encompasses everything. Nothing is like Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing.
reference: Al-Lālakāʾī, Sharḥ uṣūl iʿtiqād ahl al-sunnah wa-l-jamāʿah, 1:198, report 321, 'The creed of Abū Zurʿah and Abū Ḥātim'.
note: Ibn Abī Ḥātim reports asking both scholars about their belief and the teaching they encountered among scholars in the Hijaz, Iraq, Syria and Yemen. This is a paragraph from their joint statement. Its conclusion quotes Qur’an 42:11.

title: Abū al-ʿĀliyah and Mujāhid, cited by al-Bukhārī — أبو العالية ومجاهد عند البخاري
arabic: قال أبو العالية: ﴿استوى إلى السماء﴾ ارتفع، ﴿فسواهن﴾ خلقهن. وقال مجاهد: ﴿استوى﴾ علا على العرش.
translation: Abū al-ʿĀliyah said: 'istawā ilā al-samāʾ' means 'rose'; 'fa-sawwāhunna' means 'created them'. Mujāhid said: 'istawā' means 'rose above the Throne'.
reference: Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, Kitāb al-Tawḥīd, chapter 22, 'His Throne was upon the water', chapter-heading reports immediately before ḥadīth 7418.
note: Two early explanations quoted without full chains in al-Bukhārī’s chapter heading. They are scholarly reports, not the Prophet’s words or the text of hadith 7418. Abū al-ʿĀliyah comments on “istawā ilā al-samāʾ”; Mujāhid comments on istiwa over the Throne.

title: ʿUthmān ibn Saʿīd al-Dārimī — عثمان بن سعيد الدارمي
arabic: وعلمنا يقينا بلا شك أن الله فوق عرشه فوق سماواته كما وصف، بائن من خلقه.
translation: We know with certainty, without doubt, that Allah is above His Throne, above His heavens, as He described, distinct from His creation.
reference: ʿUthmān ibn Saʿīd al-Dārimī, al-Radd ʿalā al-Jahmiyyah, Dār Ibn al-Athīr edition, p. 44, discussion of the verses of highness and Qurʾān 58:7.
note: The author’s own explanation in al-Radd ʿalā al-Jahmiyyah. The adjacent discussion reads the accompanying mentioned in Qur’an 58:7 in light of Allah’s knowledge. This is ʿUthmān ibn Saʿīd al-Dārimī, distinct from the author of the well-known Sunan.

title: Agreement reported by Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr — ابن عبد البر
arabic: لأن علماء الصحابة والتابعين الذين حملت عنهم التآويل في القرآن قالوا في تأويل هذه الآية: هو على العرش وعلمه في كل مكان، وما خالفهم في ذلك أحد يحتج بقوله.
translation: The scholars among the Companions and Successors from whom explanations of the Qurʾān were transmitted said in explaining this verse: He is over the Throne, and His knowledge is in every place. No one whose statement is counted as authoritative disagreed with them in this.
reference: Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr, al-Tamhīd, 7:138–139, discussion of the ḥadīth of descent and Qurʾān 58:7.
note: Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr reports agreement among the early authorities in Qur’anic explanation whose statements he regards as authoritative. The verse under discussion is 58:7. His original wording is preserved; this is an attributed report about those early scholars.

title: Agreement reported by al-Sijzī — أبو نصر السجزي
arabic: أئمتنا كسفيان الثوري، ومالك، وحماد بن سلمة، وحماد بن زيد، وسفيان بن عيينة، والفضيل، وابن المبارك، وأحمد، وإسحاق متفقون على أن الله سبحانه بذاته فوق العرش، وعلمه بكل مكان.
translation: Our imams, such as Sufyān al-Thawrī, Mālik, Ḥammād ibn Salamah, Ḥammād ibn Zayd, Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah, al-Fuḍayl, Ibn al-Mubārak, Aḥmad and Isḥāq, agree that Allah, exalted is He, is Himself above the Throne, and His knowledge is in every place.
reference: Al-Sijzī, al-Ibānah, as quoted by al-Dhahabī in al-ʿUluw li-l-ʿAliyy al-Ghaffār, entry 569, 'Abū Naṣr al-Sijzī'.
note: Al-Sijzī reports agreement among the named imams. Al-Dhahabī immediately clarifies that “bi-dhātihi” (“Himself”) is al-Sijzī’s explanatory wording, attributed to those imams by meaning. It is not presented as the independently verified exact phrase of every named imam.

title: Consensus reported by Ibn Taymiyyah — ابن تيمية
arabic: وأجمع عليه سلف الأمة: من أنه سبحانه فوق سمواته على عرشه علي على خلقه، وهو سبحانه معهم أينما كانوا يعلم ما هم عاملون.
translation: The early generations of the community agreed that He, exalted is He, is above His heavens, over His Throne, high above His creation; and He is with them wherever they are, knowing what they do.
reference: Ibn Taymiyyah, al-ʿAqīdah al-Wāsiṭiyyah, in Majmūʿ al-fatāwā, 3:142.
note: Ibn Taymiyyah explicitly attributes this consensus to the Salaf. The same sentence joins Allah’s highness with His knowledge of His creation. This entry records his historical claim within al-ʿAqīdah al-Wāsiṭiyyah.

title: Ibn Abī Zayd al-Qayrawānī — ابن أبي زيد القيرواني
arabic: وأنه فوق عرشه المجيد بذاته، وهو في كل مكان بعلمه.
translation: He is Himself above His glorious Throne, and He is in every place through His knowledge.
reference: Ibn Abī Zayd, al-Risālah, opening chapter on obligatory beliefs; text reproduced in ʿAqīdat al-salaf: Muqaddimat Ibn Abī Zayd al-Qayrawānī li-kitābihi al-Risālah, printed p. 56.
note: From the creed opening al-Risālah, reproduced on printed p. 56 of the linked edition. The quotation belongs to Ibn Abī Zayd’s text. Later Mālikī commentators differed in explaining this phrase; the reading presented here is the Athari one.

title: Ibn Qudāmah — ابن قدامة
arabic: فإن الله تعالى وصف نفسه بالعلو في السماء، ووصفه بذلك محمد خاتم الأنبياء.
translation: Allah Most High described Himself as being on high, above; and Muḥammad, the Seal of the Prophets, described Him in that way.
reference: Ibn Qudāmah, Ithbāt ṣifat al-ʿuluww, introduction, printed p. 63 in the linked edition.
note: From the author’s introduction. “Fī al-samāʾ” is rendered according to the Athari understanding of being on high; it does not mean that a created heaven contains Allah.

title: Ibn Taymiyyah — ابن تيمية
arabic: وما ذكر في الكتاب والسنة من قربه ومعيته لا ينافي ما ذكر من علوه وفوقيته، فإنه سبحانه ليس كمثله شيء في جميع نعوته، وهو علي في دنوه قريب في علوه.
translation: What the Book and Sunnah mention of His nearness and His being with His creation does not contradict what they mention of His highness and being above. Nothing is like Him in any of His attributes: He is high in His nearness and near in His highness.
reference: Ibn Taymiyyah, al-ʿAqīdah al-Wāsiṭiyyah, in Majmūʿ al-fatāwā, 3:143.
note: The author explains why highness and nearness do not contradict one another. The preceding passage also rejects the idea that the created heaven carries or shelters Allah.

title: Ibn al-Qayyim — ابن القيم
arabic: فمن شهد مشهد علو الله على خلقه وفوقيته لعباده واستوائه على عرشه، كما أخبر به أعرف الخلق وأعلمهم به الصادق المصدوق، وتعبد بمقتضى هذه الصفة ... فيستحيي أن يصعد إليه من كلمه وعمله ما يخزيه ويفضحه هناك.
translation: Whoever contemplates Allah's highness over His creation, His being above His servants, and His rising over His Throne, as reported by the most knowledgeable of creation about Him, the truthful and believed Messenger, and worships in accordance with this attribute ... feels ashamed that words and deeds that would disgrace him there should ascend to Him.
reference: Ibn al-Qayyim, Ṭarīq al-hijratayn wa-bāb al-saʿādatayn, Dār ʿAṭāʾāt al-ʿIlm edition, 1:88–89, discussion of inward sufficiency through knowing Allah's attributes.
note: From the author’s discussion of how knowing Allah’s attributes shapes worship. The ellipsis marks an omission. “Contemplates” describes the heart’s awareness, not physically seeing Allah.

title: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Bāz — عبد العزيز بن باز
arabic: ومعنى استوى: ارتفع وعلا، وهو استواء يليق بجلال الله.
translation: Istiwa means rising and being above, in a manner befitting Allah's majesty.
reference: Ibn Bāz's official website, fatwa 10872, explanation of istiwāʾ.
note: A brief excerpt from the official fatwa. The fuller answer affirms Allah’s highness and knowledge while rejecting resemblance to created beings.

title: Muḥammad ibn Ṣāliḥ al-ʿUthaymīn — محمد بن صالح العثيمين
arabic: الرحمن على العرش علا علواً خاصاً يليق بجلاله.
translation: The Most Merciful rose above the Throne with a particular elevation befitting His majesty.
reference: Ibn ʿUthaymīn's official website, Nūr ʿalā al-darb answer, content 8047.
note: A brief excerpt from the official transcript. The fuller answer distinguishes this particular istiwa over the Throne and explicitly denies that Allah needs the Throne.
